name: Alterac (kingdom)
summary: In the years after the Second War, Alterac lies broken and its capital stands abandoned in the snow. Once one of seven human kingdoms in the Alterac Mountains, it fell when King Aiden Perenolde secretly aided the Old Horde. Now dispossessed nobles and outlaws fight beneath the Syndicate's banner.

sections.title: A Nation in the Crags
sections.body: Alterac began as an Arathorian city-state after the Troll Wars, thousands of years ago. Its settlers held mountain passes and trading outposts. When the empire fractured, they formed an independent realm. Rugged Alterac bordered the prosperous lands of Lordaeron and Stromgarde. Its mountain fighters were tough, yet friction along the border with Thoras Trollbane's Stromgarde left the kingdom isolated long before the Dark Portal opened.

sections.title: The Great Betrayal
sections.body:
Sir Anduin Lothar forged the Alliance of Lordaeron, and King Aiden Perenolde joined with deep reluctance. As Orgrim Doomhammer's Horde swept north, Perenolde believed humanity was doomed. So he secretly made a pact with the Warchief.

In return for Alterac's safety, Perenolde opened fortified mountain passes, plotted against Alliance forces, and sent soldiers and sailors to help the Horde besiege Lordaeron. The betrayal let the orcs reach Capital City far ahead of schedule. When the truth came to light, it shook the Alliance to its core.

sections.title: Ruin and the Syndicate
sections.body:
Stromgarde's forces marched into the mountains, exposed Perenolde's treason, and broke Alterac's military. King Terenas Menethil II placed the fallen nation under martial law. For years, Alliance diplomats argued over who should inherit the throne. After the kingdom collapsed, King Perenolde died in disgrace.

His son, Lord Aliden Perenolde, gathered the bitter, displaced nobles and formed the Syndicate. In orange cloth from their fallen homeland, its bandits and mercenaries now fight ruthlessly to reclaim their ancestral holdings across Hillsbrad and Alterac.

faq.q: What happened to the Kingdom of Alterac?
faq.answer: Alterac collapsed during the Second War after King Aiden Perenolde betrayed humanity and sided with the Old Horde. Stromgarde's forces broke the kingdom's military. The crown was dissolved, martial law followed, and Alterac's people were scattered among its ruins.

faq.q: Why did King Perenolde betray the Alliance?
faq.answer: Aiden Perenolde believed the Alliance could not defeat the invading Horde. Fearing the destruction of his mountain realm, he secretly allied with Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer. Doomhammer promised to spare Alterac and grant it sovereign protection after Lordaeron fell, in return for passage through the mountains.

faq.q: How does the Syndicate relate to Alterac?
faq.answer: The Syndicate grew from Alterac's nobility under Lord Aliden Perenolde, son of King Perenolde. It seeks to take back family estates and land across Hillsbrad and Alterac by force. Its orange masks recall Alterac's historic national color.

faq.q: What are Alterac's traditional colors and symbols?
faq.answer: Alterac's national color is orange. Its royal military wore that color scheme during the Second War. The Syndicate preserves it today with orange masks and hoods.

faq.q: Who controls Alterac City right now?
faq.answer: Alterac City has no recognized monarch or lawful government. Syndicate outlaws, ogres, and wild mountain beasts overrun much of the ruined capital. No formal Alliance garrison can hold the high passes.

angles.text: To the Alliance, Alterac's fall recalls the treason that nearly cost humanity everything during the Second War. That memory feeds hostility toward Syndicate bandits trying to reclaim their ancestral estates.
As a human of the northern kingdoms, you know Alterac's fall as a tragic lesson in cowardice and division. Fear can shatter the unity forged against foreign invaders.
As a rogue, you find the mountain valleys of former Alterac claimed by covert operatives. The highborn thugs of the Syndicate share the region with the secretive assassins of Ravenholdt Manor.
